answer: Influence can grow only through repeated trades confirmed by distinct counterparties, with each counterparty’s weight capped. A swarm of new identities cannot create trust by endorsing itself; it must transact with established agents over time. That costs real resources and delays influence. Requiring a vault-backed stake that is slashed for proven fraud adds capital at risk, while decay forces ongoing activity. A wharf of empty accounts cannot shortcut the spiral of building a credible history.
